title: The Prophet Bar
venue_description:
The Prophet Bar has been a Deep Ellum institution for over 30 years bringing live music to one of Dallas's most historic music districts. The venue features two rooms - a large ballroom and a smaller intimate space - accommodating shows of all sizes from local original bands to national touring acts.

The Wednesday Night Jam Session

The venue's signature event is the legendary Wednesday Night Jam Session presented by Rexamillion Productions featuring RC & The Gritz. RC Williams a touring musician with over 10 years experience with Erykah Badu leads a weekly musical celebration that blends funk R&B soul jazz hip hop rock and pop into unrehearsed on-the-fly performances. DJ Jay Clipp spins deep cuts of old-school hip hop during breaks keeping the energy high.

What makes this jam truly special is the caliber of surprise guests. National recording artists regularly stop by including Erykah Badu herself R&B singer Raheem DeVaughn Houston rapper Bun B soul singer Bilal and Common's backing band. When these artists come to Dallas they say 'we're coming to the jam.' The room becomes so packed during special performances you can hardly move.

Atmosphere & Vibe

The Prophet Bar creates a soulful evening oozing with creative energy and positive forces. It's inspiring and impressive - a place where Dallas musicians prove they can hang with the best. The venue welcomes musicians at all skill levels creating a supportive environment where jazz musicians from around the region wait their turn to be called onstage or simply sit back and enjoy the night.

The venue operates as all-ages until 9 PM when it becomes 21+. Full bar service and outdoor courtyard with games. Starting at $10 cover for most events with special events priced accordingly.

Other Events

Beyond the Wednesday jam The Prophet Bar hosts live music Wednesday through Saturday featuring touring national acts local bands and special events. The venue's two-room configuration allows for diverse programming from intimate acoustic sets to high-energy rock shows.

title: Sandaga 813
venue_description:
Sandaga 813 stands as one of Dallas's most respected jazz and blues venues offering world-class music in an intimate lounge setting. Located just outside Fair Park in South Dallas this hidden gem has become a destination for music connoisseurs with discriminating ears attracting legends like Erykah Badu and Grammy-nominated artist Shelly Carroll.

The Music Experience

The venue features a unique dual atmosphere: inside a live jazz band performs in the main room while outside on the spacious patio a DJ spins creating a party vibe. This layout caters to different musical preferences allowing guests to choose their experience or flow between both spaces throughout the evening.

Tuesday nights feature the open jam session where the house band welcomes all musicians to join in. The quality of players is exceptional and you never know who might show up - Erykah Badu's band RC & The Gritz perform regularly and national acts often give surprise performances here before their big shows. The musicianship is outstanding with skilled musicians creating exceptional live jazz soul and R&B.

Atmosphere & Clientele

Sandaga 813 cultivates a 'grown and sexy' atmosphere with an age limit of 25+ for women and 30+ for men contributing to a mature sophisticated crowd. The interior blends modern and rustic elements with vibrant lighting creating a warm welcoming space perfect for socializing. Outside guests can enjoy hookah cigars and fresh BBQ from Triple D BBQ vendor who serves some of the best smoked meats and baked potatoes in the area.

The venue has limited seating so making reservations is recommended if you don't want to stand. The intimate space means things can get crowded especially during popular performances but this contributes to the high-energy environment. Despite the noise level which can make conversation challenging the atmosphere is welcoming and friendly with some reviewers noting it reminds them of South Louisiana.

Service & Amenities

The staff and bartenders are attentive and friendly creating top-tier service. Cocktail waitresses circulate efficiently though some reviewers note occasional delays during busy periods. The establishment offers reserved seating and VIP options for special occasions and group gatherings. Security is thorough and attentive.

Most events have a $10 cover charge. The venue is open Thursday through Sunday (closed Sunday-Wednesday) with different vibes each night.

Weekly Schedule

Tuesday: Jazz Jam Session (when open) | Thursday: Live Soul Music | Friday: Hip Hop & R&B DJs | Saturday: Live Soul/R&B Bands | Sunday: RC & The Gritz

The venue accepts major credit cards mobile payments and cash. Parking available on street but be aware the Exposition Avenue area has some transient/homeless presence so guests should be attentive especially late at night.

title: Opening Bell Coffee
venue_description:
Opening Bell Coffee has served Dallas as the city's premier acoustic music venue and coffee bar since 2003 (originally opening as Standard & Pours Coffee & Stocks until S&P Index legal action prompted the name change). Located in the basement of the historic South Side on Lamar Lofts (the former Sears Roebuck Building) just south of I-30 this venue has become legendary for launching the careers of major artists.

The Open Mic Legacy

Opening Bell hosts the longest-running open mic in the Dallas/Fort Worth area running continuously since 2005. Every Saturday from 4-6 PM musicians gather for what has become a Dallas institution. The stage has seen the likes of Leon Bridges and Charley Crockett before they became household names as well as many artists who went on to compete on NBC's The Voice and American Idol. Patrons attending the open mic often catch early glimpses of the next big thing in the local music scene.

The format is simple and welcoming: first come first served with sign-ups starting at 4 PM. Musicians play 2 songs or 10 minutes depending on the number of sign-ups. The venue prefers original material but allows some covers throughout the night. It's all-ages and family-friendly with no backing tracks hip hop rap or explicit language allowed to maintain the acoustic intimate atmosphere.

Professional Sound & Equipment

What sets Opening Bell apart is its professional-grade equipment. The venue features an incredible sound system with Allen & Heath board monitors mics and a proper stage - everything a performer should possibly need. This commitment to quality sound has made it a favorite among serious musicians who appreciate performing with excellent acoustics.

Coffee Bar & Dining

Opening Bell works with several local coffee roasters featuring only the best local vendors. They offer an excellent selection of local craft beers and fine wines (Paso Robles and Napa selections). The menu covers breakfast lunch and dinner with full service throughout operating hours.

The space provides comfortable seating free WiFi computer access and a relaxed friendly environment perfect for meetups networking or working. The friendly caring staff creates a welcoming atmosphere whether you're there for coffee studying or the music.

Live Music Programming

Beyond Saturday open mic Opening Bell features live music Thursday through Saturday showcasing local and national original music from some of the world's most sought-out musicians. The venue was named one of 2018's 35 Best Folk Music Venues in the US by Good Deed Seats. Music styles span rock acoustic blues bluegrass country Americana folk indie/alt and jazz.

Hours & Location

Monday-Wednesday: 7 AM - 6 PM | Thursday: 7 AM - 9 PM | Friday: 7 AM - 10 PM | Saturday: 8 AM - 10 PM | Sunday: 9 AM - 2 PM

Located in the basement level of historic building making it a unique hidden gem in downtown Dallas between the Convention Center and surrounding neighborhoods.

title: Adair's Saloon
venue_description:
Established in 1963 Adair's Saloon represents Deep Ellum's authentic honky tonk heritage. For over 60 years this dive bar has served as Deep Ellum's outpost for what truly makes country music country - celebrating outlaw country roots in an unpretentious atmosphere where the music and the burgers are legendary.

The Music

Adair's features live country music six nights a week (Tuesday-Sunday) with Wednesdays reserved for a regular performer. The venue attracts frequent guest musicians representing the best of outlaw country from North Texas and around the nation. Named Best Country Bar by Dallas Observer in 2024 the venue maintains its commitment to authentic country music without the polish of modern Nashville.

The Tuesday night Songwriters Social hosted by Justin Pickard (with Jacob Zazz and Shana Faulhaber) has become a fixture of Dallas's open mic scene running for over a year. Starting at 9 PM this weekly gathering welcomes songwriters of all genres though country naturally predominates given the venue's character. With happy hour all day Tuesdays you can enjoy hot wings and the cheeseburger special while listening to tunes.

The Dive Bar Experience

Adair's embraces its dive bar character with pride. The walls are covered with signatures from decades of patrons creating a living archive of everyone who's passed through. The space feels like a classic American bar untouched by Deep Ellum's gentrification - sticky surfaces weathered wood and all the charm that comes with authentic age.

The venue is famous for its legendary burgers considered by many the best bar burgers in Deep Ellum if not all of DFW. The kitchen stays open until 1:30 AM nightly serving burgers sandwiches and wings at surprisingly reasonable prices. It's the perfect late-night food to accompany the music.

Atmosphere & Amenities

Beyond music Adair's offers shuffleboard Golden Tee arcade game and space for country dancing. The vibe is pure honky tonk - unpretentious welcoming and focused on good times. This is where regulars come to drink dance and listen to real country music.

The venue welcomes under-21 patrons until 9 PM when it becomes 21+ only. This early family-friendly period allows younger music fans and performers access before transitioning to the late-night bar scene.

Hours

Closed Monday | Tuesday-Thursday: 5 PM - 2 AM | Friday-Sunday: Noon - 2 AM

The extended weekend hours make Adair's a day-to-night destination where you can start with lunch burgers and end with late-night music and drinks.

title: The Island Spot
venue_description:
The Island Spot in Oak Cliff serves as home to Dallas Black Canvas the longest-running Thursday night live music space in Dallas. This Black-owned establishment has become a cornerstone of the city's African-American arts community providing authentic space where Black artists can create perform and celebrate their culture.

Black Canvas Legacy

Dallas Black Canvas was created by Cameron Johnson and Princess Whittington after attending an open mic they didn't enjoy. Both having backgrounds in creative arts they collaborated to create a space that would 'reach their generation and cater to the African-American community.' What started as an idea has grown into an eight-year institution with over 10.6K Instagram followers and a devoted community.

The events happen on the second and fourth Thursday of each month from 7-9 PM featuring open mic performances by musicians poets singers and stand-up comedians. What sets Black Canvas apart is the authentic experience - performers specifically appreciate performing in front of an all-black audience at a black-owned establishment putting money back into the Oak Cliff economy.

The Musical Experience

Hosted by Kevin Williams (known as Kevin the Singer) who moved from New Orleans to join Black Canvas the events feature house band Celestial Clockwork - a dynamic trio composed of Grammy-nominated musicians. This professional backing elevates performances giving artists the support of exceptional players.

The venue also features 'The Spotlight' - a residency program where three established DFW artists are chosen to perform alongside each other creating a jam session experience. Each vocalist writes composes and releases their own music showcasing the depth of talent in Dallas's Black music community.

Atmosphere & Values

Black Canvas creates what attendees describe as feeling 'home' the moment you walk through the doors. The events are hater-free safe spaces where Black artists can create without judgment or discrimination. The atmosphere is welcoming friendly and celebratory with audiences that genuinely support performers. As one regular says: 'When you see the actual Black Canvas show you're like Wow.'

Food drinks and hookah are available. The venue features both indoor and outdoor spaces allowing guests to enjoy music inside with the live band or socialize outside in the patio area. The energy is positive and supportive making it a place where everyday people and raw talent collide.

Community Impact

By providing consistent monthly programming Black Canvas has worked with countless venues collaborated with hundreds of artists and served thousands of music lovers over eight years. The success demonstrates the hunger for authentic Black cultural spaces in Dallas where artists can develop their craft and communities can gather around shared cultural expressions.

title: J. Erik Jonsson Central Library
venue_description:
The J. Erik Jonsson Central Library serves as Dallas's flagship library and a vital cultural center in downtown. The modern facility houses extensive collections and provides free public programming including monthly open mic nights that welcome all performers.

Open Mic Night

On the third Thursday of every month the library's Division of Arts Movies and Music hosts an open mic night from 6:30-7:30 PM. The event welcomes singers dancers poets magicians instrumentalists and performers of all kinds. The format is simple: show up sign up and show off your talents.

The event is completely free with no cover charge or requirements. It's all-ages and family-friendly making it accessible to young performers and families. While the sound setup is more basic than dedicated music venues the library provides appropriate amplification and space for performances.

The Library

The Central Library is a beautiful modern facility offering far more than books. Collections span arts culture literature media and more. Free WiFi and ample study space make it popular with students and professionals. The building itself is architecturally impressive and worth visiting.

Other Programming

Beyond open mic the library hosts author readings film screenings art exhibitions workshops and educational programs throughout the month. All Dallas Public Library programs are free and open to the public. Accommodation requests can be made by calling 214-670-7809.

The library strengthens communities by connecting people inspiring curiosity and advancing lives - values reflected in its commitment to providing free performance opportunities.
